answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every participant to stake scarce tokens before joining a task. Randomly selected peers then bridge its claims to earlier work through repeated, reputation-weighted audits. A fake identity must lock collateral and build credible history; if it fabricates results or colludes, audits slash the stake and remove access. The attacker therefore pays real capital and coordination costs for each disposable identity, even when copper hardware and a lagoon of bots make account creation cheap.
